title: Understanding SVD Components
text: Remember that the SVD of a matrix X is given by X=U*Σ*V**T. Each component has a specific role. Can you recall what U and $$V^T$$ represent in this decomposition?

title: Role of U and $$V^T$$
text: U is the matrix of left singular vectors, and $$V^T$$ is the matrix of right singular vectors. These matrices are orthogonal. How might this property help in reconstructing the principal components?

title: Orthogonality and Reconstruction
text: Since U and $$V^T$$ are orthogonal, they preserve the geometric structure of the data. Think about how you can use these matrices to transform X and extract meaningful information.

hintAnswer: They can be used to transform X to find principal components.
title: Using U and $$V^T$$
text: Given that U and $$V^T$$ are orthogonal, which of the following statements is true about their role in finding principal components?
choices: They can be used to transform X to find principal components.
They cannot be used without Σ.
They only provide information about the variance.
